title: The tall head meets the stick
literal_meaning: A stick on the tall person’s head.
meaning_odia: ଉଚ୍ଚରେ ଥିବା ମୁଣ୍ଡ ଉପରେ ଠେଙ୍ଗା ପଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ଯିଏ ଆଗରେ ରହେ ବା ନେତୃତ୍ୱ ନିଏ, ତାଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ, ଚାପ ବା ଆପତ୍ତି ମଧ୍ୟ ଆସିପଡ଼େ। ଏଠାରେ ଶରୀରର ଉଚ୍ଚତାକୁ ରୂପକ ଭାବରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଉଛି।
explanation: The head that stands higher is the one pictured receiving the stick. Read editorially, prominence brings exposure: the person who leads may also receive the pressure, complaints or blame. The image describes that burden without making punishment deserved.
usage_example: Original imagined example: After volunteering to coordinate a festival, someone becomes the first person everyone approaches with complaints. A friend recalls the tall head and the stick to describe the burden of taking the lead.
cultural_context: ଡେଙ୍ଗା and ଠେଙ୍ଗା form the compact rhyme. The source gives no explicit verb; the placement of the stick on the head is enough to suggest the blow and its figurative pressure.

graphic.alt: A central figure holding a plan touches his head beneath a raised stick while others crowd around with papers and gestures.
graphic.caption: An imagined burden of prominence gathers pressure around the person in front.

odia_summary: ଆଗରେ ରହିବା ସହିତ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଓ ଚାପ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆସେ।
english_summary: The person who stands foremost also faces the pressure.
